findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher checks the wrong characters and the condition is inverted
findings.body: The context prefix is 6 chars (session type 0-1, token type 2-3, grant type 4-5), but the matcher reads `substring(3, 5)`, which is the second char of the token type plus the first char of the grant type. The comparison is also negated: it returns false when the substring equals the expected shortcut. A token id with the correct grant shortcut therefore fails to match at the correct position. The only thing the matcher effectively verifies is the `xxx:UUID` shape, so the expectedGrantShortcut argument is not really validated. The fix is `substring(4, 6)` with `!equals` → return false. The comment 'starts at 4th char' also contradicts the 0-based indices used.

findings.title: Null check for rawTokenId validates grantType instead
findings.body: The fourth `Objects.requireNonNull` call passes `grantType` but carries the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed'. A null `rawTokenId` is therefore accepted. Later `encodeTokenId` would produce a token id ending in the literal string `:null`, and `getTokenContextFromTokenId` would never produce it. The check must use `rawTokenId`.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
findings.body: `getShortcut()` is added as an abstract method on a public server SPI interface (no default). Every third-party grant type factory fails to compile or throws AbstractMethodError at runtime. Worse, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` calls it on all grant factories, and a null or duplicate shortcut from a custom grant would either NPE on ConcurrentHashMap.put or abort server startup. A default method, or null-safe handling in the encoder, would avoid this.

findings.title: Context copy constructor removed and grantType captured only once
findings.body: The public `Context(Context)` copy constructor is removed from an SPI class, which breaks any caller or extension that used it. `grantType` is read from `formParams` once in the constructor, while `setFormParams(...)` can replace the form params afterwards without updating `grantType`. The grant type used for the token id could then differ from the actual request parameters.

findings.title: Token type derived from session context client rather than the client the token is issued for
findings.body: `getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)` reads `session.getContext().getClient()`. `TokenManager.initToken` receives an explicit `client` argument, which can differ from the context client (for example token exchange or pre-authorized code, where the context client is changed). The lightweight/regular flag encoded in the id could then be inconsistent with the token actually built. It is better to pass the client explicitly.
